anf_compare.notes: No published English was consulted; translated from the PG 76 Greek only.

bible_refs.note: πνεῦμα ... κατὰ τὰς γραφάς; Cyril already quoted Πνεῦμα ὁ Θεός from John 4:24 in ep-open.
πληροῖ γὰρ οὐρανὸν καὶ γῆν restates the verse quoted in ep-rem-early.
κατ' εἰκόνα Θεοῦ πεποιῆσθαι τὸν ἄνθρωπον; LXX Genesis 1:27 καὶ ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν ἄνθρωπον, κατ' εἰκόνα θεοῦ ἐποίησεν αὐτόν.

choices.term: οὐχ ἑκὼν μᾶλλον, ἀλλὰ παρ' αὐτῶν ἠναγκασμένος
choices.english: Not willingly, but because they have forced me.
choices.why: The words finish the clause begun in ep-rem-early; nothing is added (an earlier 'I do so' was dropped).
rejected: I do so not willingly, but under compulsion from them.

choices.why: 'Muzzled' is the literal image; 'silenced' gives the sense in dignified English.

choices.english: let them stop speaking against God
choices.why: Present imperative with μή forbids an action already going on.
Cyril speaks of the divine nature as spirit (John 4:24), not of the Holy Spirit as a Person.

edition.locus: Ep remainder, middle ('Not willingly' to 'the power to rule')

pass_a_gloss: [I have become] foolish (ἄφρων), not willing rather, but having been compelled by them. Let them be muzzled (ἐπιστομιζέσθωσαν) then, those babbling these things, as unlearned (ἀμαθεῖς), and let them be quiet, not touching the things beyond [their] power, or rather let them not speak against (καταλαλείτωσαν) God. For God is above all creation, neither being conceived as body, nor in bodily types or shapes, but he is simple, immaterial, formless, uncompounded (ἀσύνθετος), not composed of parts or limbs or members just as we [are], but rather spirit, according to the Scriptures, and overseeing all things, being everywhere and filling all things, and left lacking by nothing; for he fills heaven and earth. But the [saying that] man has been made according to the image (κατ' εἰκόνα) of God has other significations (ἐμφάσεις) and senses. For he alone beside all the animals on earth is rational, compassionate (φιλοικτίρμων), having fitness toward every virtue, and having been allotted (λαχών) also to rule [continues in the next section: over all things on earth].
pass_b_english: Not willingly, but because they have forced me.
So let those who babble such things be silenced, as the ignorant people they are; let them keep quiet and not meddle with what is beyond their power, or rather, let them stop speaking against God.
For God is above all creation: he is not conceived as a body, nor in bodily forms or shapes.
He is simple, immaterial, without form, and not composite; he is not put together from parts, limbs, or members as we are.
Rather, as the Scriptures say, he is spirit (John 4:24); he looks upon all things, is present everywhere, fills all things, and is absent from nothing.
For he fills heaven and earth (Jeremiah 23:24).
The statement that man was made in the image of God (Genesis 1:27) bears another sense and points to another meaning.
For of all the living creatures on earth he alone is rational and compassionate, with an aptitude for every virtue, and he has also been given the power to rule.
source_text:
ἄφρων, οὐχ ἑκὼν μᾶλλον, ἀλλὰ παρ' αὐτῶν ἠναγκασμένος. ἐπιστομιζέσθωσαν
τοίνυν οἱ ταῦτα φλυαροῦντες, ὡς ἀμαθεῖς, καὶ ἠρεμείτωσαν μὴ ἁπτόμενοι τῶν ὑπὲρ
δύναμιν, μᾶλλον δὲ μὴ καταλαλεί 605 τωσαν τοῦ Θεοῦ. ὁ γὰρ Θεὸς ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν
κτίσιν ἐστὶν, οὔτε σῶμα νοούμενος, οὔτε ἐν τύποις ἢ σχήμασι σωματικοῖς, ἀλλ' ἔστιν
ἁπλοῦς, ἄϋλος, ἀνείδεος, ἀσύνθετος, οὐκ ἐκ μερῶν ἢ μελῶν ἢ μορίων συγκείμενος
καθάπερ ἡμεῖς, πνεῦμα δὲ μᾶλλον, κατὰ τὰς γραφὰς, καὶ τὰ πάντα ἐφορῶν,
πανταχοῦ ὢν καὶ τὰ πάντα πληρῶν, καὶ οὐδενὸς ἀπολιμπανόμενος· πληροῖ γὰρ
οὐρανὸν καὶ γῆν. τὸ δὲ κατ' εἰκόνα Θεοῦ πεποιῆσθαι τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἑτέρας ἐμφάσεις
καὶ ὑπονοίας ἔχει. μόνος γὰρ αὐτὸς παρὰ πάντα τὰ ἐπὶ γῆς ζῷα λογικός ἐστι,
φιλοικτίρμων, ἐπιτηδειότητα πρὸς πᾶσαν ἀρετὴν ἔχων, λαχὼν δὲ καὶ τὸ ἄρχειν

review_notes: Replaces a scaffold row that held no translation; the English is new, translated from the locked PG 76 Greek in translations/ac_ep_rem_source.json.
Reviewer rv0 fix applied: the added 'I do so' removed, so the section opens 'Not willingly, but because they have forced me.'
Negations kept: 'not conceived as a body, nor in bodily forms', 'not composite', 'not put together', 'absent from nothing'.
John 4:24, Jeremiah 23:24 and Genesis 1:27 checked against the verses.
